content.thinking: I need to fix root_cause so it doesn't name the revision, and correct "a week" in CF-2. Checking the got_lucky note about whether the month turned — since Oct 17 to Oct 24 is clearly within the same month, I'll leave that detail as is.

action_items.item: After rolling back or deploying the fix, run scripts/repair_monthly_totals.py from draft pull request #334: export the accounts, run a dry run first, then apply and write the corrected totals back. A rollback alone keeps adding to totals that are already short.
Run the spend-integrity reconciliation much more often than its current schedule, so totals that drift from their purchases are flagged soon after a deploy.
Link the SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert to on-call paging so a person is paged when it fires.
Add a review rule: a change that stops writing a stored field must first move every reader of that field off it, and the reviewer checks this against the code that reads it.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' stored spend-this-month totals fell short of their recorded purchases: {A1} of {A2} shopper totals did not reconcile, the widest was short by {A3}, and the oldest affected purchase was recorded at {A4}.

Purchases recorded since then were written without moving the stored monthly total. At the running revision, record_purchase appends the purchase and adds to total_cents only, and leaves total_this_month_cents where it was.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 4c810f2 at {P1.1}: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at {A4}, after the later deploy of 26f1d7e at {P2.1}.
A flag change, for example switching on the derive_the_month write path: the flag provider showed {T14.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus in the {T14.3} hour before {T14.4}.

causal_chain.step: The change behind this is the deploy of revision 26f1d7e at {P2.1}. Its diff removes the conditional addition to total_this_month_cents from record_purchase, on the premise that the month's figure adds up from the purchase history whenever it is needed. As of {T11.1}, all {T11.2} replicas were running that revision.

The change's premise did not hold, because the shop still keeps and uses the stored figure instead of working the month out from the purchases. The module that ran describes the account as carrying two running totals, kept on purpose instead of figures derived on demand, and says nothing in it notices when one copy moves without the other. According to Code-Fix's reading of the files that ran, spend_summary's average_spend_per_item_this_month divides the stored total_this_month_cents, and spend_reconciliation compares the stored figure against the purchases. That comparison is the check that fired.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A software change stopped the shop updating each shopper's saved "spent this month" figure when they bought something, but the shop still kept that figure, so it fell further behind their real purchases with every sale.

contributing_factors.factor: No test or review check was seen that would confirm recording a purchase leaves the stored monthly total in line with the purchases. The change removed the code that kept the total up to date while the stored figure was still kept and compared.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test asserting that reconciliation finds no disagreement after a purchase is recorded would have failed on revision 26f1d7e before it was deployed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The only thing seen to find this fault is the spend-integrity check, which runs every {A5} days. Requests kept succeeding and no metric moved, so nothing else caught the wrong totals.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A reconciliation that ran more often would have flagged the short totals soon after the deploy, before days of purchases had been written short.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile was not linked to on-call paging, so no person was paged when it fired, even though the rollback is left for a person to do.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A paged on-call engineer could have acted on the recommended rollback as soon as the alert fired, which would have stopped more totals being written short.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

got_lucky: The month had not turned between the onset and the alert. The proposed repair script rebuilds totals from each purchase's current in-month marker, so it can still rebuild this month's correct figure; after the month turned it could not rebuild the affected month's totals.
went_well: Argus formed candidate causes naming the deploy of revision 26f1d7e within {T12.1 - alert_raised} of the alert, with the onset placed at the first affected purchase.
Argus did not roll back itself, because nothing would show whether the rollback worked within the time it waits; it recommended the rollback for a person instead.
Code-Fix opened draft pull request #334, with a fix, tests and a repair script, within {T19.1 - alert_raised} of the alert.

input.root_cause: The change made record_purchase append the purchase and add to total_cents, but stop adding the price to total_this_month_cents. The account still stores total_this_month_cents as its own copy of the month's spending, and nothing on this write path brings it back in line with the purchases, so every current-month sale recorded afterwards left that stored total short by the price of the sale.
input.still_at_risk: While revision 26f1d7e runs, every current-month purchase keeps leaving shoppers' saved monthly totals short, and totals that are already short stay wrong until they are repaired; the write path behind the derive_the_month choice in the code that ran also leaves the month total unchanged in the same way.
input.symptom: Shoppers' stored spend-this-month totals fell short of the purchases recorded against them
